notes:
Context: large contact-center vendor powering omnichannel support for multiple retail brands. Priority is real-time agent assist that integrates with their CTI and internal ticketing. Key asks: streaming suggestions (token-by-token), sub-150ms p95 latency for suggestion surface, deterministic guardrails for canned responses, and robust fallback when GPUs are saturated during marketing-driven spikes.

Key quotes / call snippets:
- 'We need suggestions that don't lag — agents will ignore anything >200ms.' — Director of CX Ops
- 'Tool calling must be auditable; every API action logged and reversible.' — Head of Integrations

Technical requirements summary:
- Workload: high-rpm short-turn interactions (avg response 2–6 tokens suggested, high concurrency during promos)
- Latency SLO: p50 < 60ms, p95 < 150ms for the streaming suggestion endpoint
- Throughput target: baseline 2k concurrent agent sessions; spike to 10k for 30–60 minute windows (Black Friday style)
- Model preferences: open to quantized Llama-variant or Redwood-verified models; want deterministic low-latency variants for live assist and cheaper larger-context variants for post-call summarization
- Routing/fallback: prefer regional routing NA primary, EU fallback; automatic downgrade to smaller-quantized model when CPU/GPU oversubscription detected; circuit-breaker + partial-suggestion strategy
- Security/compliance: Okta SSO/SAML, SCIM user provisioning, encrypted-at-rest KMS, audit logging for every tool call, 7-year retention for transcripts for legal team (discuss retention controls)
- Integrations: Genesys/Avaya CTI connectors, internal ticketing via REST, Wire-level monitoring integration (CloudWatch/Datadog)

POC scope (agreed):
- 2-week POC running in Redwood Dedicated pool mimicking production traffic profile
- Implement streaming suggestions endpoint with guardrails for profanity and PHI redaction
- Run spike tests to 10k concurrent sessions using provided harness; capture token-level latency, percentiles, and cost metrics
- Validate tool-calling audit trails with sample ticket-update flows (idempotency checks)

Open questions / risks:
- Legal: standard contract redlines required (data residency clauses)
- Okta SCIM mapping: they require group-scoped roles (need mapping docs from SE)
- Cost: they asked for detailed token-level vs seat-based pricing scenarios for spikes
